summary.headline: Time Technoplast Q2 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 32% to ₹996 crore, EBITDA up 80% to ₹265 crore, PAT up 27% (transcript figures as stated, partly garbled).
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with H1 FY27 net sales up 29%, EBITDA up 17% and PAT up 25%, driven by pass-through of input prices and mix. Composite products grew 29% in H1, and management reiterated 15% minimum volume growth with EBITDA growth above 20% and PAT growth above 25%. Capex of ₹174 crore was incurred in H1, with a planned ₹375 crore for the year partly offset by ₹134 crore of non-core asset sales. Management also flagged a 14.2 kg LPG cylinder delay, a deferred acquisition of a US packaging entity, and a merger of a subsidiary effective 1 April 2026. The transcript is machine-garbled in places, so several figures are as stated and should be verified against the filing.

segments.name: Industrial packaging (drums, jerricans, IBC, pails)
segments.commentary: Management guides 11–13% growth (around 12%) for this segment. Management also said a subsidiary has started IBC manufacturing, with potential business of ~₹100 crore over 3 years.

segments.name: Composite products (LPG, CNG, hydrogen, fire extinguisher)
segments.commentary: Segment grew 29% in H1 FY27 per management; guidance is 25–30% growth. Management cited a shortage-driven shift by OMCs to composite cylinders for new LPG connections.

segments.name: PVC/HDPE pipes (water, sewage, drainage, power ducts, gas lines)
segments.commentary: Guidance 20–25% growth. Management said H1 is seasonally weak (about 35–40% of pipe business), with H2 at 60–65%, and that state-level price revisions are easing contractor payment delays.

segments.name: Other products (marks film, auto components, start-up matting, lifestyle)
segments.commentary: Small share of business; guidance 10–12% growth.

segments.name: Overseas operations
segments.commentary: Revenue grew ~27% with overseas capacity utilisation ~86%. Management said revenue is split across Middle East (~11%), Southeast Asia (~18%) and USA (~9%).

guidance_outlook: Minimum 15% volume growth YoY for at least the next 3 years; with 15% volume growth, EBITDA growth is expected above 20% and PAT growth above 25%.
Composite products expected to grow 25–30%; management estimates composite business of ₹800–900 crore this year, ₹2,500 crore in 3 years and ₹4,000 crore in 5 years.
Net capex of about ₹250 crore after non-core asset sales; post-FY27 capex limited to maintenance and brownfield, up to ~₹250 crore.
Targeted annual ROCE improvement of 1.5–2%; EBITDA margin improvement of 1–1.5% from automation and consolidation, implying ~15.5% margin next year from ~13.3%.
Solar power savings of ~₹11 crore this year, expected to double to ₹22–25 crore next year.
Management expects H1 to be about 45% of full-year revenue, EBITDA and PAT, and says it will surpass guidance.
capex_capacity: Capex in H1 FY27 was ₹174 crore; planned FY27 capex is ~₹375 crore, with ~₹134 crore from non-core asset sales expected, leaving a net ~₹250 crore.

Morai (Maharashtra) composite plant completed, with automated equipment for CNG/hydrogen cylinders; existing equipment from Dhamman and Siddhasa to be consolidated there, using ~25,000 sq ft. Management said expansion takes 6–8 months.
Greenfield fully automated project completed in ~2 months and commercialised, located ~40 km from Mumbai (product not clearly named in transcript).
Overseas capacity utilisation ~86%; India utilisation ~83%, with management saying expansion is needed beyond 90% sustained for 6 months.
Management said 6–7 more locations are under consideration for consolidation; 6 manufacturing locations were consolidated last year.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices (HDPE/PP) rising on West Asia conflict and freight; management said pass-through to customers occurs with a 20–25 day lag.
Management said LPG new connections for steel cylinders are suspended, with OMCs offering new connections only in composite cylinders; supply shortage is constraining the LPG market.
CNG cascade order book reported as strong; management said the automotive cylinder segment was previously capacity-constrained and is now opening.
Pipe business: management said state governments are revising prices, and H2 seasonally stronger; contractors were earlier delayed in payments.
Management said it stays with 10–12% margins and does not pass on large price increases to IPC contractors, using price-variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 15% volume growth guidance supported by capacity completion at Morai and IBC, and what is the expansion trigger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expansion starts when utilisation is above 90% for 6 months; the Morai plant is ready and consolidates Dhamman and Siddhasa equipment. Hydrogen commercialisation timing depends on demand, with clarity expected mid to end 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the composite business growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the company as the only Indian firm with PESO-approved type 4 composite cylinders, LPG shortage and OMC shift to composite cylinders for new connections, and cascade demand. Management said it is entering the automotive cylinder segment after capacity expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the pending QIP proceeds and the pipe business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹220 crore of QIP funds is pending, with ~₹75 crore of automation spend under way and an expected 1% EBITDA benefit. On pipes, management said price revisions and government payment timing are improving and H2 is seasonally stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any inventory gain or loss in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory is held at 65–70 days and that there was no inventory gain or loss in Q1 or Q2. Foreign exchange impact is typically under 0.5% of value.

risks_watch: Acquisition of a US packaging company (QIP-funded) was not completed; management said it has been deferred for 2–3 years given the war situation and underperformance versus expectations.
Management said the 14.2 kg LPG cylinder development is delayed by 3–4 months due to geopolitical uncertainty and capex deferral.
Pipe business: seasonal weakness in Q2 (monsoon) and contractor payment delays; H2 recovery depends on state price revisions.
Raw material and freight volatility from West Asia and Russia-Ukraine conflicts; pass-through lag of 20–25 days.
Management's large capex plan (₹1,250 crore for ₹5,000 crore revenue) is contingent on hydrogen demand; hydrogen cylinder commercialisation timing unclear.
Transcript contains garbled and inconsistent figures (for example, H1 revenue and PAT, and overseas growth); verify against the filing before relying on them.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on composite growth, capacity and multi-year targets, with many specific numbers. Less precise on the acquisition, pipe-business timing and the 14.2 kg cylinder, where delays were acknowledged, and some answers were deflected to later updates.
key_quotes: So that definitely continues to give us the growth though the overall LPG situation in this current scenario is tight but our business continues to grow.

Yeah, you are correct and once again I would like to reclaim again we are the only company in India who is in type 4 composite cylinder which is approved by the Peso and very well accepted in the market since the last three years.

And definitely when the volume growth is 15% and the EBITDA growth will be more than 20% and PACE growth will be more than 25%.
